bio: Barbara Jean Lee (née Tutt; born July 16, 1946) is an American politician who has served as the 52nd mayor of Oakland since 2025. A member of the Democratic Party, Lee previously served as a U.S. representative from California from 1998 to 2025, representing California's 12th congressional district (numbered as the 9th district from 1998 to 2013 and as the 13th district from 2013 to 2023). She also served in both houses of the California State Legislature from 1990 to 1998.
offices: Member of the California State Assembly (1990–1996)
Member of the State Senate of California (1996–1998)
Chair of the Congressional Black Caucus (2009–2011)

items.t: Supports legislation restricting the availability of guns and took part in the 2016 House sit-in on gun violence.
items.q: Lee is a strong advocate for legislation restricting the availability of guns. She participated in the 2016 sit-in against gun violence in the House of Representatives.

items.t: Authored the Shirley A. Chisholm United States−Caribbean Educational Exchange Act on school teacher training and community involvement in the Caribbean.

items.t: Sponsored a bipartisan bill in the House to repeal the 2001 AUMF, which passed 268–161 (2021).
items.q: In June 2021, Lee sponsored a bipartisan bill in the House to repeal the AUMF, which passed 268–161.

items.t: Called for a 10% cut to the U.S. military budget.

items.q: Lee has supported US aid to Ukraine during its invasion by Russia and has voted in favor of all bills for aid to Ukraine

items.t: Has supported legislation to expand home ownership, improve public housing quality, and assist the homeless.
